habitats: Habitable geothermal rock surfaces below approximately 70 °C
summary: A thin microbial consortium whose growth-form label describes its appearance. Sulfur oxidizers occupy moist boundaries where reduced sulfur and oxygen overlap below this consortium's fictional approximately 70 °C ceiling; green partners require cooler, adequately illuminated and chemically tolerable patches. Their bands may overlap or break apart. Hotter centres carry abiotic sulfur and may contain arsenic- and mercury-bearing crusts; colour does not establish contamination or living activity. Sosa grazes suitable margins and el_resoplido collects accessible sulfur-bearing fragments (F7, F23, F24, F26).

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: This consortium is confined to oxygenated mixing zones below approximately 70 °C. Hotter centres contain abiotic deposits, not this living film; sulfur oxidation may proceed to sulfate rather than accumulate sulfur. Strict review (2026-11-19): Residual: F7 and F23 support geothermal reduced-sulfur sources, while F5's pO₂ of approximately 0.34 bar supplies a potential oxidant. Sulfur-driven autotrophy and conditional elemental-sulfur accumulation are coherent. Residual weakness: atmospheric oxygen does not guarantee oxygen delivery inside a wet film; sulfide supply, diffusion and consumption determine the active boundary and whether sulfur accumulates or proceeds to sulfate.

analogues.mechanism: Oxidation of reduced sulfur conserves energy, with elemental sulfur appearing as an intermediate under suitable conditions.

chains.trait: Overlapping microbial patches controlled by temperature, redox conditions and light
links: Seep temperature, reduced sulfur, oxygen delivery, acidity and illumination vary over short distances.
Sulfur oxidizers occupy moist sulfur–oxygen overlap zones within their tolerated temperatures, including suitable cool patches.
Green partners occupy sufficiently illuminated, chemically tolerable surfaces at approximately 10–40 °C, a fictional placement range for this consortium.
These requirements produce overlapping or discontinuous patches rather than a compulsory green-to-warmer-oxidizer sequence.
Hot pulses kill established patches and leave mineral crust, while persistent gradients determine subsequent zonation.
chains.play: Compare living patches and abandoned mineral crusts without treating band order or colour as a safety instrument.
chains.weakness: Heat pulses, failed oxygen delivery, acidification or persistent shading can exclude living partners; visible growth does not reveal gas or metal hazards.
observe: Green patches overlap pale films only where light and cooled flow permit.
A redirected hot trickle leaves a dead strip.
Hot central crust retains colour without living tissue.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Approximately 70 °C is this fictional consortium's placement ceiling, not a universal limit for life. Reserve hotter centres for abiotic sulfur and arsenic-bearing crust in this entry; no new thermophile species is added. Strict review (2026-11-19): revised: The original imposed an unsupported warmer oxidizer band, so the rewrite supplies separate partner masks and allows overlapping, discontinuous zonation. Residual: F7 and F23 support geothermal chemical gradients, F5 supplies atmospheric oxygen, and F24 permits green photosynthetic partners. Independent overlapping habitat requirements repair the unsupported compulsory thermal sequence. Residual weakness: atmospheric oxygen does not establish delivery inside the film, and the 10–40 °C and approximately 70 °C limits are declared fictional tolerances rather than deductions from these facts. The generator explicitly acknowledges both limitations.

analogues.mechanism: Organisms with differing thermal tolerances form spatial bands as water cools away from its source.

gameplay.gift_item: Loose sulfur-bearing crust fragment for el_resoplido
gameplay.mineral_lick: Fixed specialist resource at habitable margins; unsuitable as an ordinary salt lick.
gameplay.notes: Sosa grazes suitable marginal surfaces; el_resoplido collects accessible sulfur-bearing fragments, which does not establish that the film itself is its food. Poison is null for intrinsic plant alkaloids, not a declaration that the mixed crust is edible. Raw sulfur is poisonous to ordinary consumers, and arsenic, mercury, SO₂ and H₂S remain distinct environmental hazards (F23, F26). Player_lineage can collect a specialist gift but has no established sulfur, metal or gas immunity. Living growth does not make water or air safe, and specialist feeding does not authorize access to extreme heat.

overlay_rules: Green partners appear only within their separate temperature, light and chemistry mask.
Exposed high-slope photosynthetic patches may develop stronger red-purple screening.

placement.slope: Moist seep terraces and cooled marginal channels; exclude active vent throats and living instances above approximately 70 °C.
placement.wetness: Persistent moisture and local delivery of required substrates; atmospheric oxygen alone does not establish oxygen inside a wet film.
placement.soil: Sulfur-bearing mineral-coated rock; arsenic and mercury vary by patch. Hot central deposits are abiotic terrain.
placement.fog: Optional; local geothermal moisture sustains films, while steam can reduce useful light.
placement.density: Discontinuous patches generated from separate partner masks; overlap is allowed and simple band order is not required.
placement.sulfur_oxidizer_mask: Require reduced sulfur, moisture and delivered oxygen to overlap below the fictional consortium ceiling of approximately 70 °C; do not impose a warmer-than-green requirement.
placement.photosynthetic_partner_mask: Require approximately 10–40 °C, sufficient time-integrated light for positive net growth and tolerable acidity; these are fictional partner-specific placement conditions.
placement.chemistry: Track acidity and neutralizing flow rather than imposing a universal pH range. Sulfide oxidation toward sulfate can acidify margins and weather substrate, excluding green partners where buffering is inadequate.
placement.snow: Above approximately 1,750 m in winter, retain exposed active patches only where local geothermal heat prevents snow cover; altitude alone does not guarantee snow-free ground.

generator.seasonal: Changing seep routes and runoff redraw patches; redirected heat can kill established film. Snow and light availability independently limit exposed photosynthetic growth.
generator.wind_response: Adherent film barely moves; exposed edges dry while surrounding gas plumes change direction.

journal.en: A living skin at the poisoned spring's edge. Farther in, only crust remains.
journal.es: Una piel viva al borde del manantial envenenado. Más adentro solo queda costra.
